newsitem.title: BAHRAIN: Bahrain says two Qataris held on spying charges.
newsitem.headline: Bahrain says two Qataris held on spying charges.

text.p: Bahrain said on Tuesday it had arrested two Qataris on charges of spying, the official Gulf News Agency reported.

An official source quoted by the agency said a man and a woman had confessed before an investigating judge to spying for Qatar. They were named as Fahad Hamad Abdullah al-Baker and Salwa Jassim Mohammed Fakhri.
The source said Baker and Salwa told the judge they were sent to gather information that could harm Bahrain's national security and passed it to Qatari intelligence.
Baker, who the source described as a Qatari intelligence officer, and Salwa would be tried in Bahrain, he said.
The source said Bahrain in January 1987 arrested a similar group on charges of spying for Qatar. He gave no further details.

Qatar and Bahrain are locked in a territorial dispute over a group of islands, reefs and sandbanks which are potentially valuable and of strategic importance. Qatar has taken the case to the International Court of Justice, a move which has angered Bahrain which insists on a regional solution.
